causes.text: Moderna's mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine candidate achieved 94.5% efficacy in a large Phase 3 trial, with just five infections among 30,000 vaccinated participants compared with 90 infections in the placebo group, signaling a major breakthrough and outperforming early data from rivals.

source_info.title: Moderna's COVID-19 Vaccine Candidate Meets Primary Efficacy Endpoint

effects.text: AstraZeneca's shares fell after the company announced that its adenovirus-based COVID-19 vaccine showed an average efficacy of about 70%, well below the ~95% efficacy reported by mRNA rivals, leading investors to question the vaccine's competitiveness and sell off the stock.

source_info.title: AstraZeneca shares fall after efficacy findings for COVID-19 vaccine

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Moderna announced its COVID-19 vaccine candidate was 94.5% effective, far exceeding expectations and demonstrating mRNA vaccines could reach around 95% efficacy.

Investors compared this high efficacy to AstraZeneca's viral-vector vaccine candidate and began to view AstraZeneca's product as less competitive relative to mRNA vaccines, raising concerns about its commercial prospects.
When AstraZeneca released data showing only about 70% efficacy, its stock fell about 3.8% as investors reacted to the comparatively lower efficacy.

rationale: The cause event-Moderna's announcement of very high vaccine efficacy-set a performance benchmark. Investors subsequently judged AstraZeneca's vaccine efficacy against this benchmark; when AstraZeneca's data were lower, confidence waned and the share price dropped.
counterfactual_analysis: Had Moderna's vaccine not demonstrated such high efficacy, expectations for COVID-19 vaccine performance would have been lower, and AstraZeneca's 70% efficacy might not have been viewed so unfavorably, possibly averting the share price decline.

adversarial_confounders.text: Broad market volatility during the pandemic
adversarial_confounders.impact: Global stock market swings unrelated to vaccine data could also have influenced AstraZeneca's share price.

details.commentary: Aggressive competition among North American airlines kept fares under pressure even as costs for fuel and labor moved higher. Delta's cautious commentary on yields and capacity signaled that rivalry was still intense, making it harder to rebuild margins fully.

Stronger travel demand supported load factors and ancillary revenues, encouraging Delta to add back more capacity and invest in its product. As each successful quarter reinforced investor confidence in the recovery path, the positive loop between demand, profitability and balance-sheet repair supported the stock, even with periodic pullbacks.
